subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers start a state-path fix now from the paired table errors, or first require redacted runtime diagnostics proving which SQLite file each failing subsystem opened in Docker?
rationale: Source review shows both subsystems should use the same shared DB, but the observed contradiction depends on live process path resolution; choosing a fix without that proof could repair the wrong boundary.

options.title: Collect path proof first
options.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared state DB path, and `PRAGMA database_list` output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

options.title: Build a repro branch
options.body: Use the report as enough signal to create a Docker regression around gateway run, device-pair notify polling, `chat.history`, and `sessions.send` under the stated env.

options.title: Treat as broader recovery work
options.body: Fold this into shared SQLite recovery only if maintainers decide the table errors are a symptom of wider state DB detection or repair gaps.

recommendation.title: Collect path proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared state DB path, and `PRAGMA database_list` output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for shared SQLite state, plugin-state migration, and ACP SQLite metadata points to steipete.
